title: Fallback compression and late-binding admission controller for tenant-aware load-shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket proposes a combined approach to load-shedding that (1) applies tenant-aware late-binding admission decisions and (2) offers degradations that reduce token cost and tail latency via 'fallback compression' and lightweight response modes. The goal is to preserve P99 latency SLOs and overall service availability during transient multi-region capacity pressure while minimizing customer-visible quality loss and unit cost inflation.

Why this work: motivation and constraints:
- Recent multi-region incidents showed we can keep latency SLOs by shedding traffic but we lack a consistent, tenant-aware scoring mechanism and a set of low-impact degradations. Current shedding is coarse (reject/accept based on static lanes) which increases failed requests and surprises customers.
- We need a last-moment (late-binding) admission controller that uses up-to-date slot/capacity state and a set of degradations that are fast to apply (no model reloading) and measurable.
- Business constraints: maintain customer SLAs where possible; avoid blackholing traffic from high-value tenants; reduce per-token cost spike under overload.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Admission: implement a late-binding admission controller in the edge/ingress layer that scores requests on a short window of live capacity signals (region free slots, model-variant latency headroom, tenant weight, route priority). Decision outcomes: Accept; Accept+Degrade (apply compression/mode); Queue (short-lived FIFO up to 150ms); Reject (503 with soft-fail payload).

2) Degradation modes (fast, reversible, policy-driven):
- Fallback compression (primary new feature): compress generated outputs by applying a run-time sequence-compression filter. For causal generation we post-process to abbreviate predictable continuation patterns, elide filler tokens, and apply a length-limited summarization micro-pass using a local lightweight policy network (quantized 8-bit module) that runs on CPU or small GPU slice.
- Trim-context: remove least-significant system/user turns from context (preserves immediate prompt + recency).
- Verbosity-reduction: change response generation params (max_tokens, temperature) and apply structured outputs that are shorter (e.g., bullet-mode vs. long-form).
- Placeholder mode: return structured placeholder with 'high-level answer + "expand" token' that can be expanded asynchronously if needed.

3) Tenant-aware scoring: each request gets a composite score: S = alpha*(tenant_priority) + beta*(route_priority) + gamma*(1 - recent_error_rate) + delta*(headroom_fraction). Score thresholds determine outcome. Rates and thresholds are configurable per-dedicated pool / customer-tier.

4) Telemetry & SLOs: expose per-tenant metrics for acceptance rate, degrade-rate, P50/P95/P99 latencies, token-cost delta, user-error-rate. The admission controller emits events for every decision to enable auditing and offline ML calibration.

Engineering details and trade-offs:
- Late-binding timing: controller must run within the first 10ms of request to avoid adding tail. We will co-locate it with the ingress and implement a lightweight C++ path with existing admission hooks.
- Fallback compression quality vs CPU: compression micro-pass must be cheap (<5ms avg) and should be opt-in per model variant. For customers on Dedicated we can enable a slightly heavier compression since capacity is reserved.
- Observability: need a new dashboard in Console that shows 'degradation taxonomy' and token-savings estimates by tenant.
- Safety: ensure structured placeholders do not leak prompts or PII. Compression algorithm will run through current redaction pipeline.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (spike): implement a prototype compression micro-pass (local CPU quantized) and run on 10% of low-priority traffic in region-us-west for 2 weeks. (Spike results linked below).
- Phase 1 (canary): implement late-binding admission controller in ingress, route 5% of production through it enabling only 'trim-context' and 'verbosity-reduction'.
- Phase 2 (gradual): enable fallback compression for low-priority tenants and measure user-visible quality regressions via eval prompt set.
- Phase 3: full policy release with console controls and per-tenant configurability.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- P99 E2E latency remains within SLO (target: <= 2.2x baseline) under the simulated overload test at 75% degradation of global capacity.
- Degrade mode reduces average token consumption by >= 22% for affected requests.
- Customer-visible error rate (503s) decreases by >= 30% compared to baseline shedding.

Links to artifacts and experiments:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/Fallback+Compression+Design
- Spike notebook & benchmark: https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2b3c-fallback-spike
- Draft PR for micro-pass (github): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7891
- Admission controller prototype (repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/compare/late-binding-admission

Open questions / known unknowns:
- Compression micro-pass quality: what evaluation prompts best reflect customer UX? PM to provide golden set.
- Cost modeling: need tighter estimate for CPU cost vs token savings; initial spike shows 0.12 CPU-seconds per 1k compressed requests.
- Multi-region coordination: how to share headroom info across regions without adding coordination latency? Consider gossip with 100ms staleness tolerance.

Next steps:
- Diego: finalize prototype implementation plan and break into sub-tasks (implementation + infra + eval) by 2026-03-05.
- PM (Marta Chen): assemble evaluation prompt set and success criteria by 2026-03-10.
- Infra: allocate 3 small test pools in us-west/us-east/eu-west for canary by 2026-03-15.

Customer impact: medium (degradation rather than rejection is expected to improve availability for most tenants).
comments: 2026-03-03: Spike complete. Fallback compression reduced median tokens by 18% and P99 generation time by ~10ms in the local benchmark. Trade-off: occasional semantic compression errors on highly technical prompts.
2026-03-04: Design review with PM, Product, and Security. Security flagged PII risk; we've added redaction pass and audit logging requirement.
2026-03-06: Infra notes: ingestion needs a non-blocking admission hook; agreed to embed decision in request metadata to avoid extra RTTs.
2026-03-08: Engineering sync: prefer implementing late-binding logic in C++ path inside ingress to hit 5-10ms target. Diego to open infra ticket for canary pools (ENG-42795).
2026-03-10: PM provided evaluation set (see drive link). Initial manual review shows acceptability threshold ~80% for non-critical tenants.
2026-03-12: Security review scheduled; added security_review_required flag and formal threat model task.
